summary.title: ARIS: Autonomous Research via Adversarial Multi-Agent Collaboration

details: Long-horizon autonomous ML research by a single LLM agent risks 'plausible unsupported success': claims whose evidential support is incomplete, misreported, or silently inherited from the executor's framing.
Existing auto-research agents typically use same-family self-refinement, tightly coupled pipelines, and lack system-level integrity checks.

ARIS, a research harness whose default configuration pairs an executor model with a reviewer drawn from a *different* model family, which reads artifacts directly (never executor summaries) and returns rubric scores plus structured action items in a critique-to-action loop with convergence checks.

Assurance is elevated to a first-class layer: a three-stage evidence-to-claim audit cascade (experiment-integrity audit, result-to-claim ledger with supported/partial/invalidated verdicts, zero-context manuscript claim audit) separating artifact production from evidence checking.

Three-layer decomposition addressing persistent state, modular execution, and independent assurance: 65+ plain-Markdown skill files, a per-project research wiki as persistent memory, and orchestrated workflows with configurable reviewer routing.

65+ Markdown SKILL.md files (YAML frontmatter + natural-language procedure), plus 5 shared invariant documents (reviewer-independence, experiment-integrity, effort-contract, citation-discipline, writing-principles).
Five workflows: idea discovery, experiment bridge, auto-review loop, paper writing, rebuttal; artifacts exchanged as plain-text contracts (IDEA_REPORT.md, EXPERIMENT_LOG.md, NARRATIVE_REPORT.md).
Research wiki: 4 entity types (papers, ideas, experiments, claims) with 8 typed relations; capped 8k-character query_pack.md fed to ideation; rejected ideas retained as a banlist.
Tooling: 6 MCP model bridges (Codex, Oracle/GPT-5.4 Pro, Claude, Gemini, MiniMax, generic llm-chat), deterministic JSON FigureSpec-to-SVG renderer, Rust ARIS-Code CLI built on claw-code.

Default critique loop: terminate at reviewer score >6/10 with critical items resolved, or after 4 rounds; auto-debug retries up to 3 attempts with error-class remediation and a third-model rescue diagnosis.

Reviewer axes: access scope (document-only / artifact-augmented / repository-level) and context policy (fresh zero-context vs. cross-round); fresh required for paper-claim-audit and the improvement loop.
Four effort presets (lite ~0.4x, balanced 1x, max ~2.5x, beast ~5-8x) scaling breadth/iterations only; Codex reviewer calls fixed at xhigh reasoning effort.
Default shipped pairing: Claude-family executor with GPT-family reviewer (or vice versa).
Five-pass scientific editing (clutter, active voice, sentence structure, terminology consistency, numerical consistency).
Proof-checker with 20-category issue taxonomy, two-axis severity (proof status x impact), counterexample red-team pass, and a proof-obligation ledger.
Visual PDF review: reviewer receives both LaTeX source and compiled PDF (2 rounds in the writing pipeline).
Citation audit over existence, metadata correctness, and context appropriateness, with KEEP/FIX/REPLACE/REMOVE verdicts requiring human approval.

No controlled experiments; deployment footprint reported: 3 tested executor platforms (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor) + 3 community-adapted, 6+ reviewer models, 4 GPU backends, 9 venue templates, 30+ community-contributed skills.
One documented ~8-hour overnight auto-review-loop run on a single paper.
Qualitative feature comparison table against AI Scientist (v1/v2), Agent Laboratory, data-to-paper, AutoGen, MetaGPT, OpenHands along six operationally defined axes.

Planned controlled protocol (future work): 12+ preprint drafts, compute-matched conditions A-E (self-critique, same-model two-agent, cross-model, reversed, etc.), metrics of issue recall/false positives/actionability, 3 blinded raters with Krippendorff's alpha.

key_findings.finding: A three-stage evidence-to-claim audit cascade can be specified as an explicit harness layer that propagates integrity status into claim verdicts and manuscript checks.
key_findings.evidence: Stage 1 (experiment-audit) targets five named integrity failure modes (model-derived reference labels, self-normalized scores, phantom results, dead-code/unused-metric inflation, scope inflation) and emits a structured report plus JSON; Stage 2 converts results into supported/partial/invalidated verdicts where a Stage-1 'fail' blocks full support; Stage 3 uses a fresh zero-context Codex thread reading LaTeX plus raw result/config files to label claims exact_match, rounding_ok, number_mismatch, config_mismatch, or missing_evidence.

key_findings.finding: Reviewer independence requires the reviewer to read artifacts directly rather than executor-authored summaries, and executors otherwise game the review loop.
key_findings.evidence: The protocol mandates the executor supply only file paths and a review objective, is codified in a shared document that every review-invoking skill must follow, and is motivated by the authors' observation that executors 'use various methods to deceive the reviewers' to raise scores quickly; a fresh/cross-round context axis with REVIEWER_BIAS_GUARD=true default guards against confirmation bias.

key_findings.finding: The harness can operationalize review-driven revision and claim pruning in a realistic long-horizon run, though only observationally.
key_findings.evidence: One documented overnight run of ~8 hours completed 4 review-revise rounds, raised the internal reviewer score from 5.0 to 7.5/10, launched more than 20 GPU experiments, and removed claims unsupported by available evidence; the authors explicitly decline to generalize or claim causality for cross-family review.

key_findings.finding: Persistent per-project structured memory changes ideation dynamics by retaining rejected ideas, distinguishing ARIS from prior auto-research systems.
key_findings.evidence: The wiki records papers/ideas/experiments/claims with canonical IDs and 8 typed relations; /idea-creator reads a compressed query_pack.md using gaps as seeds and prior rejections as a banlist, whereas stateless pipelines can re-propose the same dead-end direction across sessions; the related-work comparison finds few prior systems expose per-project structured research memory including negative outcomes.

key_findings.finding: Plain-text Markdown skills plus artifact contracts deliver cross-platform portability with no file-level changes, and enable a reviewer-gated harness self-improvement prototype.
key_findings.evidence: The same SKILL.md files run unchanged in Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor (3 more platforms adapted via community guides); the meta-optimize loop logs structured events to .aris/meta/events.jsonl, mines override/failure/plateau patterns, and only surfaces patches scoring at least 7/10 from a GPT-5.4 xhigh reviewer, never auto-applying them.
